s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Skin biopsy showed histiocytes, lymphocytes, foam cells, multinucleated giant cells, eosinophils, and hemorrhage
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities, and specific histiocytic infiltrate pattern

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by granulomatous skin lesions and potential systemic involvement, including endocrine abnormalities

shortlist.label: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with skin lesions and potential multisystem involvement, although less commonly associated with endocrine abnormalities

shortlist.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and potential endocrine involvement, with histiocytic infiltrate

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease. The skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis with histiocytes, lymphocytes, foam cells, multinucleated giant cells, eosinophils, and hemorrhage, and immunohistochemical results negative for CD1a and S-100 but positive for CD68, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, which are typically positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

rejected.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match the typical features of Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma, which often involves the periorbital area and has a distinct biopsy appearance

rejected.label: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show the characteristic multinucleated giant cells with a ground-glass appearance seen in Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis

rejected.label: Adult-Onset Multisystem Histocytosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease, and Adult-Onset Multisystem Histocytosis is a less well-defined entity
